title: Robust cis-by-trans epistasis in the human plasma proteome highlights an ABO-centered interaction network.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: Europe PMC lists no open full text, no supplement, no text-mined accessions and no Zenodo/Dryad deposits; the only NCBI link is a PMC id (13636544) with no full text in Europe PMC.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From the abstract only: individual-level genotypes and plasma protein levels come from the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project (UKB-PPP); the result is 7 significant cis-by-trans epistatic effects.

a1_downloadable.note: Needs individual-level UK Biobank genotypes and proteomics, which are controlled access (UK Biobank application required). No open deposit found; checked only via the paper's metadata.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No released table of labels. The paper's output is 7 interaction hits, far too few to serve as a label set.

a5_enough_rows.note: 7 significant epistatic effects reported in the abstract; individual-level rows are inaccessible.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Biobank-scale genotypes across about 3,000 proteins would not fit, even if access were granted.

a8_label_provenance.note: Protein levels are measured with Olink proximity-extension assays, so the label is a real measurement and not another model's output.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible without access to the data. With access, the claim would be limited to whether genetic-variant interactions predict plasma protein levels in mostly European-ancestry UK Biobank participants.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use pairs of genetic variants to predict a person's blood protein levels beyond what each variant does alone.
plain_idea.train_on: Genotypes and about 3,000 plasma protein measurements per UK Biobank participant; the number of participants was not verified (data controlled).
plain_idea.predict: Plasma protein levels, measured with Olink antibody-based proximity-extension assays (a lab method that counts proteins using paired antibodies).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: This would show whether gene-gene interactions matter for protein regulation, but the authors already found only 7 robust effects and little gain.

ml_idea: Not pursued: an interaction-aware model predicting protein levels from genotypes requires controlled UK Biobank data, and the paper reports only 7 robust interactions.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; the data is inaccessible.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Is there an open download of the individual-level data? There isn't: UK Biobank requires an access application.

verdict_reason: A1 fails: the inputs and labels are individual-level UK Biobank genotypes and proteomics, which are controlled access, and the paper deposits nothing open. Its released result is just 7 interaction hits, too few to train on.
